en: 10. Indriyayamaka 10.3.
Pariññāvāra 10.3.3.
Anāgatavāra (The Chapter on the Future)
10.3.3.1. Positive Order (Anuloma) He who will fully understand the eye-faculty will abandon the faculty of mental distress?

Two persons will fully understand the eye-faculty, but they will not abandon the faculty of mental distress. Five persons will both fully understand the eye-faculty and abandon the faculty of mental distress.
Or again, whoever will abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya) will also fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? Yes.
Whoever will fully understand the faculty of the eye will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?
Six types of persons will fully understand the faculty of the eye, but they will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
Those ordinary persons who will attain the path will both fully understand the eye faculty and cultivate the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty.
Or, conversely, whoever will cultivate the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty will also fully understand the eye faculty? Yes.
Whoever will fully understand the eye faculty will cultivate the "final-knowledge" faculty? Yes.
Or again, will he who develops the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? Yes.
Will he who fully understands the faculty of the eye realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)? Yes.
Or again, will he who realizes the faculty of one who has already known fully understand the faculty of the eye?
One who possesses the path of the highest fruit will realize the faculty of one-who-has-known, but will not fully understand the eye-faculty.
Seven types of persons will both realize the faculty of one-who-has-known and fully understand the eye-faculty.
(Based on the eye-faculty.)
Will one who will abandon the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?
Four types of persons will abandon the faculty of mental distress, but they will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Those worldlings (puthujjana) who will attain the path will both abandon the faculty of mental distress and cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
Or rather, will he who develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" abandon the faculty of mental grief? Yes.
Will he who abandons the faculty of mental grief develop the faculty of final knowledge? Yes.
Or rather, will he who develops the faculty of final knowledge abandon the faculty of mental grief?

Two persons will cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), but they will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*); five persons will both cultivate the faculty of final knowledge and abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever abandons the faculty of mental grief will realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever realizes the faculty of one who has already known will abandon the faculty of mental grief?
Three persons will realize the faculty of one who has already known, but they will not abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Five persons will both realize the faculty of one who has already known and abandon the faculty of mental grief.
(Based on the faculty of mental grief.)
Is it the case that whoever will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya) will also cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will cultivate the faculty of final knowledge will also cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?
Six types of persons will cultivate the faculty of final knowledge, but they will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
Those ordinary persons who will attain the path will cultivate both the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) and the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*).
Is it the case that whoever cultivates the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" will realize the faculty of one who has known (*aññātāvindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will realize the faculty of one who has known will cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?
Seven types of persons will realize the faculty of one who has already known, but they will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Those worldlings who will attain the path will both realize the faculty of one who has already known and cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
(Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.")
He who will develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) will realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*). Yes.
Or again, he who will realize the faculty of one who has already known will develop the faculty of final knowledge?

One who possesses the supreme path (*aggamaggasamaṅgī*) will realize the faculty of one who has already known, but will not develop the faculty of final knowledge. Seven types of persons will both realize the faculty of one who has already known and develop the faculty of final knowledge. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
10.3.3.2. Negative (Paccanīka) He who will not fully understand the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya) will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya)? Yes.
Or rather, he who will not abandon the faculty of mental grief will not fully understand the eye-faculty? Yes.

Two types of persons will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet they will not fail to fully understand the faculty of the eye (*cakkhundriya*). Three types of persons will neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor will they fail to fully understand the faculty of the eye.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the faculty of the eye will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*)? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever does not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" will not fully understand the faculty of the eye? Yes.
Six persons will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," but they will not fail to fully understand the eye-faculty.
Three persons will neither cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor will they fail to fully understand the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the eye-faculty will also not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge? Yes.
Or, whoever shall not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) will not fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? Yes.
Whoever shall not fully understand the faculty of the eye will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)?

One who possesses the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) will not fully understand the faculty of the eye, yet he will not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known. Two types of persons will neither fully understand the faculty of the eye nor realize the faculty of one who has already known.

Or, whoever will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya), will that person not fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya)? Yes. (Based on the faculty of the eye.
Whoever will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya), will that person not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)? Yes.
Or, whoever will not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," will that person not abandon the faculty of mental grief?
Four types of persons will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet they will not abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Five types of persons will neither cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental grief will also not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge?

Two types of persons will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet they will not fail to cultivate the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*). Three types of persons will neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor will they cultivate the faculty of final knowledge.
Or, is it the case that whoever does not cultivate the faculty of final knowledge will also not abandon the faculty of mental grief? Yes.
Whoever will not abandon the faculty of mental grief, will he also not realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)?

Three persons will not abandon the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), yet they will not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*). Two persons will neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor will they realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Is it the case that whoever does not realize the faculty of one who has already known will also not abandon the faculty of mental grief? Yes. (Based on the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*) will also not cultivate the faculty of higher knowledge (*aññindriya*)?

Six persons will not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," but they will not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*). Three persons will neither develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor will they develop the faculty of final knowledge.
Is it the case that whoever will not develop the faculty of final knowledge will also not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"? Yes.
Is it the case that whoever will not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" will not realize the faculty of one who has known (*aññātāvindriya*)?
Seven persons will not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet they will not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Two persons will neither cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor will they realize the faculty of one who has already known.

Or again, will he who does not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya) not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)? Yes. (Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Will he who does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) not realize the faculty of one who has already known?

One who possesses the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) does not develop the faculty of final knowledge, yet he does not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known. There are two types of persons who neither develop the faculty of final knowledge nor realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Or, whoever will not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya) will not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)? Yes. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
